This petition is filed by the Petitioner against Respondent No.1 & 2 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 22.09.2022 at about 7.15 p.m. he had been riding XL Heavy Duty bearing Reg.No.KA64U1262 stopped on left side of the road to refill the petrol at SCCH5 petrol bunk, opp. Doddegowda Petrol Bunk, SH33 Road, Koratagere Town, Tumakuru, a motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA06EE0416 came in high speed rash and negligently and dashed against him, due to the said accident, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was taken to Government Hospital Koratagere, after firstaid he was shifted to Kanva Sri Sai Hospital Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient, for which he had spent an amount of Rs.1,50,000/ towards medicines and Rs.50,000/ towards incidental expenses.
3. At the time of the accident he was aged about 57 years, hale and healthy, working as waterman thereby earning Rs.14,000/ p.m., due to this accident he has lost his income and earning capacity.

Out of this accident crime No.235/2022 is registered against the rider of the SCCH5 motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA06EE0416 before the Koratagere Police for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC.
R1 is the insurer, R2 is owner of the said motor cycle, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence, prays to allow the petition and grant compensation of Rs.12,00,000/ with interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
4.

On service of notice, R1/insurer has appeared and filed written statement denying entire case of the petitioner, the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA06EE0416 did not possess valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident, the said motor cycle is insured with him, he is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170 of M.V.Act, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and 158(6)
of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, there was delay of 5 days in lodging the SCCH5 complaint.
Claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.
5. R2/owner has appeared and filed written statement denying case of the petitioner, claim made by the petitioner is higher, hence his petition is not maintainable.

Further he has issued policy to offending vehicle vide policy No.60420331216760001521 valid since 17.02.2022 to 16.02.2023 and it is valid as on the date of accident, further driver of the offending vehicle had valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

6. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:

sentences.text: 1. Whether Petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 22.09.2022 at about 7.15 p.m. when petitioner was riding a XL Heavy Duty bearing Reg.No.KA64U 1262, near Doddegowda Petrol Bunk SH33 Road, Koratagete Town, Tumakuru, at that time, motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA06EE0416 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
7. In order to prove his case, petitioner himself deposed his evidence as PW1, examined 2 witnesses as PW2 and PW3 and marked 23 documents as per Ex.P.1 SCCH5 to Ex.P.23 and closed his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no evidence of respondents.

8. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, then my findings on the above issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
9. Issue No.1: In order to prove his case, petitioner has deposed his evidence as PW1, in his chief examination petitioner has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.
Hence in order to avoid repetition of facts averments made in the evidence affidavit are not reiterated here.

In this regard copy of FIR is marked as SCCH5 Ex.P.1, copy of complaint is marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of seizure mahazar is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of Sec.133 notice is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of reply notice is marked as Ex.P.6, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.7,
copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.9.
10 . In crossexamination there is no dispute about place, date and time of the accident by the counsel for R1/insurer.
R2/owner has not cross examined the PW1, only denial is that, vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA06EE 0416 has not caused this accident.
Further he admits that, while crossing the road this accident is occurred, there is no zebra lane.
Further denied that, it is a false case.
Further admits that, as per the wound certificate, very accident is in between both the two two wheelers.

sentences.text: Police papers marked at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9 speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the Mariyappa who is rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA06EE0416.
On the other hand, there is no defence evidence.
Hand sketch map is not furnished by either of the parties.
Under such circumstances, it is not possible to say that, there is contributory negligence of the petitioner.
It is noticed that, petitioner has not produced his driving licence and vehicle documents.
Only on that basis, it is not possible to hold that, there is contributory negligence of the petitioner.
Hence considering the same, believing the version of the petitioner, I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.2:
As per the evidence of the petitioner, he had sustained fracture middle 1/3 clavicle SCCH5 right, for which he was operated with ORIF with LCP right clavicle.

In this regard he has furnished copy of wound certificate marked as Ex.P.8, discharge summary marked as Ex.P.10 issued by Kanva Sri Sai Hospital, wherein he took treatment as indoor patient since 23.09.2022 to 25.09.2022, referral card marked as Ex.P.14, lab report marked as Ex.P.15, Xray Films marked as Ex.P.17.
13.

Further Medical Record Officer at Kanva Sri Sai Hospital is examined as PW2 and marked notarized copy of ID card marked as Ex.P.18, copy of police intimation is marked as Ex.P.19, copy of MLC Extract is marked as Ex.P.20, case sheet is marked as Ex.P.21.
In crossexamination deposed that, he do not know about the case sheet.
Further he do not know anything about the corrections made in the case sheet.
Further he do not SCCH5 know about variations in date and time.
Further he admits that, in physical examination sheet date 23.09.2022 is corrected as 22.09.2022.
Further admits that, even in operation notes there is overwriting.
Further denied that, in order to help the petitioner documents are tampered.

14. Dr.Rajesh M.B., Consultant Orthopaedic Surgeon at Meditech Speciality Hospital is examined as PW3 and furnished assessment proforma is marked as Ex.P.22, Xray Films marked as Ex.P.23 and he has assessed permanent physical disability for right upper limb at the rate of 38%.

15. In crossexamination admits that, he has not treated the petitioner, there was no direction from this court to assess the disability, only there is directions to produce clinical notes and give evidence,
after receipt of SCCH5 summons he has assessed the disability on the basis of the information given by the petitioner.
He has gone through the xerox copies of wound certificate and discharge summary of Kanva Sri Sai Hospital, further verified the wound certificate issued by the Government Hospital Koratagere.
As per Ex.P.8, injury No.2 is grievous in nature, accident is taken place in between 2 two wheelers, but only single vehicle number bearing Reg.No.KA64U1262 is entered in injury certificate.
He has seen the discharge summary one Dr.Mahesh and his team have conducted the surgery, he has not consulted him prior to assessment of disability.
16. Fracture is united and no any complications, implants is not yet removed, he cannot say why implants is not removed.
He has already advised for removal of implants.

Further admits that,
reasons are not SCCH5 mentioned in evidence affidavit, not given calculation sheet, he has not Narashimamurthi D.K vs National Ins Co Ltd on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89519828/
4 gone through the follow up records, he has examined the movements of limbs with reference to the guidelines prior to assessing the disability,
17.

sentences.text: Further he do not know about avocation of the petitioner.
He cannot say about the expenses for removal of implants in Government hospital.
Further denied that, proper assessment can be made only after removal of implants.

Wound certificate marked at Ex.P.8 speaks that, there is abrasions over left forehead 2x2 cm, further there is light right clavicle middle bone fracture, injury No.1 is simple in nature, injury No.2 is grievous in nature.
Ex.P.10 is a discharge summary accordingly he took treatment as indoor patient in Kanva Sri Sai Hospital for 3 days, surgery is conducted with right ORIF SCCH5 + plating done under RA on 23.09.2022.

There is medical bill of Rs.93,222/.
18.

On going through the same, it is noticed that, injuries caused to the petitioner is not a scheduled injury, but as per the say of the Doctor, there is disability to the particular limb at the rate of 38%.
Looking to the oral and documentary evidence available on record, it is noticed that, there is no fracture of right shoulder as per say of the Doctor, only there is clavicle fracture.
However there is surgery and he was indoor patient for 3 days.
Furthermore petitioner is aged about 57 years old and waterman, considering the same, functional disability is considered at the rate of 7% for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

19. As per the case of the petitioner, he was aged about 57 years, for proof of his age, he has produced SCCH5 copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.16, wherein it is clearly mentioned date of birth of the petitioner is 01.01.1965 and the alleged accident is occurred on 22.09.2022, accordingly relying on Ex.P.16 his age is considered about 58 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 9 is applicable as per decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s.
Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

sentences.text: 20. As per his case, he was working as waterman, thereby earning Rs.14,000/ p.m., to prove the said fact, there are no documents on record.
Hence considering the same, this court relied upon the Karnataka Minimum Wages for the year 202223.

In the case on hand, petitioner is waterman,
nature of work is not mentioned in the petition, so that, he comes under the category of formerly groupIV - now unskilled worker category.

Very SCCH5 accident is occurred on 22.09.2022,
accordingly as on the date of accident including dearness allowances for unskilled workers minimum wages for a month will come to Rs.13,821/, so that, said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss income during laid up period and also for the purpose of calculation of loss of future income.

Keeping in mind injuries caused to the petitioner, treatment taken, expenses incurred and also the pain suffered, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, it is just and necessary to allot compensation under other heads, accordingly for pain and sufferings compensation of Rs.15,000/
is awarded, for conveyance, SCCH5 nourishment and attendant charges Rs.15,000/
is awarded,

Further petitioner is also entitled for compensation for medical expenses incurred by him, for which, he has produced medical bills marked as Ex.P.11 for an amount of Rs.93,222/.
22.

Accordingly, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below: Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount in Rs.
1.
Loss of future income 1,04,48700 2. Pain and sufferings 15,00000 3. Conveyance, nourishment and 15,00000 attendant charges 4.
Medical Expenses 93,22200 5.
Loss of amenities in life 15,00000 6.
Loss of income during laid up 13,82100 period Total 2,56,53000 SCCH5 23.
Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,56,530/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization of entire amount.

24. In the case on hand, respondent No.1 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.60420331216760001521, which is valid for the period from 17.02.2022 to 16.02.2023, the alleged accident was occurred on 22.09.2022, it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.
Further driver of the offending vehicle had valid driving license, in this regard there is no dispute by the respondents.
So that, R1/insurer is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
SCCH5 25. Issue No.3:

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,56,530/ (Rupees Two Lakhs Fifty Six Thousand Five Hundred Thirty Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.

For the reasons assigned to Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER::
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,56,530/ (Rupees Two Lakhs Fifty Six Thousand Five Hundred Thirty Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.

The Petitioner is entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through epayment directly to his account on furnishing the Bank A/c details along with address proof and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
